title: Noor and the Locker
premise: Rosalind 'Noor' Crane, a scholarship student at Aldercrest Academy, has spent four years counting days until graduation, convinced he doesn't belong in a town built around the school's oldest tradition: the Locker, where every senior leaves a letter to whoever opens it next. When his college essay prompt demands an honest answer about who he is, Noor discovers the Locker is slated for demolition by the school's board — and that his own anonymous letter, written freshman year, is still inside. To save the tradition, he must rally the unlikely family of misfits he's collected, expose why the board wants the letters buried, and finally claim an identity of his own; the book ends with Noor reading his old letter aloud at graduation, staying in town not as a prisoner but as the Locker's new keeper.
about_author: August Nystrom is a former boarding school scholarship kid who now writes stories about the places that take us in before we're ready to be taken in. He lives in a small coastal town where every door, drawer, and locker seems to hold someone's unfinished sentence.

chapters.title: The Question Nobody Can Skip
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Senior year begins with the college essay prompt that asks students to name the one thing they'd never say out loud. Noor's cynical draft essay accidentally gets read aloud in class, exposing more truth than he intended and catching the attention of Priya, the editor of the school paper. The emotional beat: reluctant vulnerability cracking open a boy who planned to feel nothing until graduation.

chapters.title: What the Locker Keeps
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with interludes from letters inside the Locker. Priya drags Noor into investigating the board's quiet vote to demolish the Locker wing, and he finds his own freshman-year letter still waiting inside — written by a boy who desperately wanted to belong. The emotional beat: grief and tenderness colliding as Noor realizes the school was never the prison; his silence was.

chapters.title: Every Letter Is a Witness
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Noor and Priya. The pair recruit the found-family misfits — the janitor who's kept the Locker for thirty years, a legacy student hiding her own letter — to publish the letters' history before the demolition vote. The board retaliates, threatening Noor's scholarship. The emotional beat: rising defiance as belonging stops being something granted and becomes something claimed together.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the graduation-eve hearing, Noor reads his freshman letter aloud, and one by one others follow, until the room understands the Locker made the town. The board relents; the tradition survives under new student keepers. Noor chooses to stay a year as its caretaker before college. The emotional beat: resolution — identity no longer deferred, home no longer a sentence being served.
